clue.text: Drop round eatery that's not starting to produce Middle Eastern food

indicators.note: the word for drop goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to drop is to fall

indicators.note: the eatery word loses its opening letter, so it is not starting

parts.note: a cafe is a small eatery

explanation.surface: A diner is told to drop round a restaurant that hasn't yet opened to get some Middle Eastern food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop round' reads as an invitation to visit, but 'round' is the container signal and 'that's not starting' beheads the eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-fried balls of ground chickpea, a staple street snack of the Levant and Egypt.

clue.text: See 7
Sponsor finally invested in drink, being more generous

indicators.note: the letter is put into the drink, invested in it like money

parts.note: lager is a drink, a type of beer

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of sponsor

explanation.surface: A sponsor putting money into a drinks firm turns out to be more generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A larger helping is a more generous one, more ample in size.

clue.text: Notes copied by rich figure confined to fringes of memory

parts.note: rich can mean highly amusing, as in 'that's rich'

indicators.note: the number is held between the outer letters, confined to them
the fringes of the word memory are its first and last letters

parts.note: one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: Banknotes copied out by a wealthy person whose memory is fading at the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterfeit currency: forged banknotes are copies of real ones.

clue.text: Lead sulphide at last found in smack

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the word for smack

parts.note: to smack or lash is to strike

indicators.note: picks the final letter of sulphide

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: lead sulphide finally turns up in a sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead sulphide' reads as a compound; 'Lead' is the definition, a dog's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's lead is the strap or cord that tethers it, a synonym.

clue.text: A man short, stuffed by other team

indicators.note: the shortened man is filled with the other piece, so it is stuffed by it
the word for man is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a chap is a man
else means other, as in 'someone else'

explanation.surface: A side playing with one man fewer is overwhelmed by the opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CHAP to CHA, which 'stuffed by' fills with ELSE: CH-ELSE-A.
explanation.definitionFit: A London football club, here a team named by example.

clue.text: Wife after nice crab salad they serve up

indicators.note: the wife letter comes after the other letters
a salad mixes its ingredients, so these letters are tossed together

explanation.surface: A wife follows a crab salad served by a team of waiters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salad' rearranges NICE CRAB; 'serve up' refers to staff serving passengers in an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight attendants serve meals and drinks to passengers in the air.

clue.text: Food shortage at sea's contained

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of these clue words

explanation.surface: A shortage of food at sea has been brought under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal plural noun for things to eat, grub.

clue.text: Present a woman's leg, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a small gift, the sort put in a Christmas sock
a leg fills the hosiery a woman wears

explanation.surface: Offering a glimpse of a woman's leg as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A little Christmas gift for the hung-up sock, and literally whatever fills a woman's hosiery.

clue.text: Switched on, star is lighter?

indicators.note: switched means changed round, so these letters swap places

explanation.surface: Once switched on, a star might be a source of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lights fires deliberately is literally a lighter, a cryptic sense.

clue.text: See 19
Burden of success for Tiger Woods?

definitions.meaning: a burden carried as a curse, like the seabird hung round the Ancient Mariner's neck
a golf score of three under par on a hole, a triumph for a golfer such as Tiger Woods

explanation.surface: The weight of expectation that comes with a famous golfer's winning streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the large seabird: Coleridge's curse, and the golf term for three under par.

clue.text: "Hey, the pesto I eat!" Twiggy envious o'er fantastic endorsement for Italian cookery, attributed to 19 9

definitions.text: endorsement for Italian cookery, attributed to 19 9

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A model, jealous over someone's lunch, exclaims about pesto in what pretends to be a celebrity food endorsement.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs over all thirty-one letters of 'Hey the pesto I eat Twiggy envious o'er'; Twiggy is a 1960s British model.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous remark credited to the Italian actress, crediting pasta for her figure: a celebrity endorsement of Italian food.

clue.text: Largest organ broke, farthest tip coming off

indicators.note: the far end of the word for broke comes off, removing its last letter

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke, having no money

explanation.surface: An organ snapped and its very tip fell off.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's outer covering is its largest organ by area and weight.

clue.text: Accidental French dramatist not entirely good — you can bet on it!

parts.note: in music a flat is an accidental, a sign altering a note's pitch

indicators.note: the dramatist's name is not given entirely, its last letter missing

parts.note: Jean Racine was a French dramatist

explanation.surface: An accidental mishap involving a French playwright who isn't quite good — and a tip to bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse racing without jumps is a major betting sport.

clue.text: Car left secured by straps, which cover the windows

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce car

indicators.note: the letter for left is held fast inside the word for straps

parts.note: to strap is to bind, so straps are binds

explanation.surface: A car with its left side strapped down, and some window coverings for good measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Window shades on a spring roller that pull down to cover the glass.

clue.text: Coming up, cat and connection with leopard primarily, providing theme

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of leopard
in a down clue, coming up reverses the words for cat and connection

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a tie is a connection or link
providing means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A cat and its links with a leopard, cropping up, provide the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring musical or literary motif, a theme.

clue.text: Issue partly cleared up in man's unconscious state

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go in the word for man's

parts.note: his means belonging to a man

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reverses the pieces before it

parts.note: a son is issue, offspring

indicators.note: partly cleared of its inside leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A man's unconscious state partially resolved an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared' empties 'partly' to PY; 'up' reverses SON+PY to YPNOS, which goes 'in' HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance-like condition induced by suggestion, an altered unconscious state.

clue.text: Poem — quit leaving it on a coach

indicators.note: the word it is leaving quit, removed from it

parts.note: taken as written, it is the part removed
a coach is a railway carriage, part of a train; to coach is to train

explanation.surface: Someone quits and leaves to catch a coach, poem in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-line stanza or poem.

clue.text: See 11
Italian player being capricious, sooner bottle-fed?

indicators.note: the bottle is fed into the rearranged letters
capricious means unpredictable, so the letters of sooner change order

parts.note: a phial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A changeable Italian sportsman who would rather have been bottle-fed as a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capricious' rearranges SOONER to SOOREN, and 'fed' puts PHIAL into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian film actress, a player in the stage sense.

clue.text: Hardy, Balfour and Isherwood — all extremely cross

indicators.note: takes the extreme first and last letters from each of the three names

explanation.surface: Three writers and a politician, Hardy, Balfour and Isherwood, are all furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross between two breeds or varieties is a hybrid.

clue.text: Unhinged fasteners

explanation.surface: Fasteners that have come loose from their hinges.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for crazy, and the threaded pieces that hold bolts in place.

clue.text: Walking about, army on manoeuvres touring Leatherhead

indicators.note: the rearranged letters travel round the head letter, enclosing it
an army on manoeuvres moves around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: the head of 'Leather' is its first letter, L; Leatherhead is also a Surrey town

explanation.surface: An army on exercise walks about, passing through the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ABOUT ARMY tours L, the head of 'Leather'. 'Walking about' looks like the definition, but 'about' is needed as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone able to walk, as an ambulatory patient on their feet.

clue.text: Brought up without the social graces, I maintained harmony

indicators.note: the I is maintained, held inside
in a down clue, brought up reverses the word

parts.note: non-U is a British term for language or manners not used by the upper class

explanation.surface: Someone raised without manners says they kept the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: NON-U, the British label for lower-class usage, reverses to UNON with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Union means unity or agreement, a state of harmony.

clue.text: Something afoot, say? Get away!

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a shoe is something on a foot

explanation.surface: Something is going on, people say — clear off!
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation used to drive away animals or people.

clue.text: See 11
Content of sandwich, ordinary divine fluid

indicators.note: the letters sought are contained within the run of these two words, its content

explanation.surface: The filling of an everyday sandwich turns out to be heavenly liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the ethereal fluid flowing in the veins of the gods instead of blood.

clue.text: Thus accepting demise, French leaders leaving party

indicators.note: the word for thus takes in the word for demise, accepting it inside

parts.note: so means thus, as in 'and so it was'
a demise is an end, a death
F abbreviates French; doubled it gives two Fs, leaders of the French

explanation.surface: French politicians quit their party, so accepting their downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts END inside SO; FF is two F abbreviations for French.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell gathering held for someone departing, such as a colleague moving on.

clue.text: Scrooge sending back smoke and drink

indicators.note: both words are sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: a drag is a puff on a cigarette, a smoke
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A miser refuses the cigarette and the drink he is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Scrooge is the archetype of a mean, stingy person.
